questions.stem: A car travels at 60 km/h for 2.5 hours. What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Distance = Speed × Time = 60 × 2.5 = **150 km**. **Short Trick:** 60 × 2 = 120; 60 × 0.5 = 30; total = 150 km.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A bus covers 240 km in 4 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 240 ÷ 4 = **60 km/h**. **Short Trick:** 240 ÷ 4 = 60 directly.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train travels 180 km at a uniform speed of 45 km/h. How long does the journey take?
questions.explanation: Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 180 ÷ 45 = **4 hours**. **Short Trick:** 180 ÷ 45 = 4.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train 100 m long travels at 36 km/h. How many seconds does it take to pass a telegraph pole?
questions.explanation: Speed = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s. Time = 100 ÷ 10 = **10 seconds**. **Short Trick:** Multiply km/h by 5/18 to get m/s; divide length by speed.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Convert 72 km/h into m/s.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Convert 15 m/s into km/h.
questions.explanation: 15 × (18/5) = 15 × 3.6 = **54 km/h**. **Short Trick:** Multiply m/s by 3.6 to get km/h.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A cyclist rides at 40 km/h. How far will he travel in 5 hours?
questions.explanation: Distance = 40 × 5 = **200 km**. **Short Trick:** Direct multiplication.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two trains, 120 m and 80 m long, approach each other on parallel tracks at 60 km/h and 40 km/h respectively. How long do they take to cross each other completely?
questions.explanation: Relative speed (opposite) = 60 + 40 = 100 km/h = 100 × 5/18 = 250/9 m/s. Total length = 200 m. Time = 200 ÷ (250/9) = 200 × 9/250 = **7.2 seconds**. **Short Trick:** Opposite directions → add speeds; total length ÷ relative speed.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train 200 m long passes a platform 300 m long in 25 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanation: Total distance = 200 + 300 = 500 m. Speed = 500 ÷ 25 = 20 m/s = 20 × (18/5) = **72 km/h**. **Short Trick:** Speed (m/s) × 3.6 = km/h.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two trains start from the same station at the same time, travelling in the same direction at 40 km/h and 60 km/h. After 3 hours, how far apart are they?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 60 − 40 = 20 km/h. Distance apart = 20 × 3 = **60 km**. **Short Trick:** Same direction → subtract speeds; multiply by time.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two towns are 360 km apart. A person sets out from one town at 50 km/h and another from the other town at 70 km/h, both travelling toward each other. After how many hours will they meet?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 50 + 70 = 120 km/h. Time = 360 ÷ 120 = **3 hours**. **Short Trick:** Opposite directions (approaching) → add speeds; divide distance by relative speed.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A person covers the first half of his journey at 40 km/h and the second half at 60 km/h. What is his average speed for the entire journey?
questions.explanation: Equal distances → Average Speed = 2uv/(u+v) = (2 × 40 × 60)/(40 + 60) = 4800/100 = **48 km/h**. **Short Trick:** Harmonic mean formula 2uv/(u+v); always less than arithmetic mean (50).
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A boat travels at 15 km/h in still water. The speed of the current is 3 km/h. What is the boat's downstream speed?
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = boat speed + current speed = 15 + 3 = **18 km/h**. **Short Trick:** Downstream = u + v; Upstream = u − v.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A boat's upstream speed is 10 km/h and downstream speed is 14 km/h. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.explanation: Speed of stream = (Downstream − Upstream) ÷ 2 = (14 − 10) ÷ 2 = **2 km/h**. **Short Trick:** Stream speed = (D − U)/2; Boat speed = (D + U)/2.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A and B start from the same point at the same time in the same direction. A runs at 8 km/h and B at 6 km/h. After how long is A exactly 1 km ahead of B?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 8 − 6 = 2 km/h. Time = 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5 h = **30 minutes**. **Short Trick:** Same direction → relative speed = difference; time = gap ÷ relative speed.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train passes a telegraph post in 10 seconds and a bridge 250 m long in 35 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanation: Let length = L. Speed = L/10 = (L + 250)/35. So 35L = 10(L + 250) → 35L = 10L + 2500 → 25L = 2500 → L = **100 m**. **Short Trick:** Set up equal-speed equation: L/t₁ = (L + bridge)/t₂; solve for L.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Car X covers 360 km in 4 hours. Car Y covers 300 km in 3 hours. What is the ratio of the speed of Car X to Car Y?
questions.explanation: Speed X = 360 ÷ 4 = 90 km/h. Speed Y = 300 ÷ 3 = 100 km/h. Ratio = 90:100 = **9:10**. **Short Trick:** Speed ratio = (d₁ ÷ t₁):(d₂ ÷ t₂); simplify by HCF.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two towns P and Q are 25 km apart. A and B start walking toward each other from P and Q at 4 km/h and 6 km/h respectively. After how many hours do they meet?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 4 + 6 = 10 km/h. Time = 25 ÷ 10 = **2.5 hours**. **Short Trick:** Approaching each other → add speeds; time = distance ÷ relative speed.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train 150 m long runs at 54 km/h. A man is running in the opposite direction at 6 km/h. How long does the train take to pass the man completely?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 54 + 6 = 60 km/h = 60 × (5/18) = 50/3 m/s. Time = 150 ÷ (50/3) = 150 × 3/50 = **9 seconds**. **Short Trick:** Opposite directions → add speeds before converting to m/s.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A person travels 60 km at 30 km/h and then another 60 km at 20 km/h. What is the average speed for the entire 120 km journey?
questions.explanation: Total time = 60/30 + 60/20 = 2 + 3 = 5 h. Average speed = 120 ÷ 5 = **24 km/h**. Also: 2uv/(u+v) = 2×30×20/50 = 1200/50 = 24. **Short Trick:** Equal distances → harmonic mean 2uv/(u+v).
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two trains start simultaneously from stations P and Q toward each other. After passing each other, the first train takes 9 more hours to reach Q, and the second train takes 4 more hours to reach P. What is the ratio of the speed of the first train to the second?
questions.explanation: For trains meeting and then continuing: v₁:v₂ = √t₂ : √t₁ = √4 : √9 = 2 : 3. So the first train's speed : second train's speed = **2:3**. **Short Trick:** Speed ratio = √(after-time of opponent) : √(after-time of self) = √4:√9 = 2:3.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A thief runs at 8 m/s. A policeman starts chasing when the thief is 100 m ahead. The policeman runs at 10 m/s. How long does the policeman take to catch the thief?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 10 − 8 = 2 m/s. Time = 100 ÷ 2 = **50 seconds**. Verify: In 50 s, policeman covers 500 m; thief covers 100 + 400 = 500 m. ✓ **Short Trick:** Same direction → relative speed = difference; time = head start ÷ relative speed.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A boat takes 4 hours to row upstream and 2 hours to row the same distance downstream. The speed of the current is 2 km/h. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.explanation: Let boat speed = v. Since distance is equal: 4(v−2) = 2(v+2) → 4v−8 = 2v+4 → 2v = 12 → v = **6 km/h**. Verify: upstream speed=4 km/h, downstream=8 km/h; distance=4×4=16 km; 16÷8=2 h ✓. **Short Trick:** Same distance upstream/downstream → equate (t_up)(u−v) = (t_down)(u+v).
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Three friends A, B, and C run around a circular track of 1200 m in the same direction. Their speeds are 300 m/min, 200 m/min, and 150 m/min respectively. After how many minutes will all three meet at the starting point for the first time?
questions.explanation: Time for A to lap B = 1200 ÷ (300−200) = 12 min. Time for A to lap C = 1200 ÷ (300−150) = 8 min. Time for B to lap C = 1200 ÷ (200−150) = 24 min. All three meet after LCM(12, 8, 24) = **24 minutes**. **Short Trick:** Lapping time = track ÷ relative speed; all meet at LCM of pairwise lapping times.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A motorboat whose speed in still water is 12 km/h takes the same time to travel 30 km upstream as it does to travel 42 km downstream. What is the speed of the current?
questions.explanation: Let current speed = x. 30/(12−x) = 42/(12+x) → 30(12+x) = 42(12−x) → 360+30x = 504−42x → 72x = 144 → x = **2 km/h**. Verify: 30/(12−2)=3 h = 42/(12+2)=3 h ✓. **Short Trick:** Equal-time equation → cross-multiply and solve for x.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
